summary: Best-of-breed June-2026 research + adversarial verify + synthesis for the Starlight Voice Operator voice loop

dimensions.choice: Keep Pipecat — the artifact's preference is still correct for June 2026. Build the local primary loop as a Pipecat pipeline: LocalAudioTransport (PyAudio/WASAPI) -> local STT (Whisper or NVIDIA Parakeet on CUDA) -> OpenRouterLLMService (global doctrine, streaming) -> local TTS (Kokoro preferred for naturalness/latency, Piper as the ultra-low-resource fallback), with LocalSmartTurnAnalyzerV3 for semantic end-of-turn + barge-in. Push-to-talk (Ctrl+Shift+Space) gates the transport input; wake-word added later via the same input stage.
corrections: Latency target is hardware-optimistic as stated. The ~520-650ms first-audio figure derives from datacenter GPUs (Kokoro 45ms-first-chunk is measured on an RTX 5090); Frank's GTX 1650 (Turing, 4GB, no Tensor cores) will be materially slower. P50<=800ms first-audio is plausible but not comfortable on this laptop; P95<=1500ms is at genuine risk once OpenRouter provider TTFT tail variance stacks on local STT+TTS GPU contention. Do not present ~520ms as 'this hardware class with headroom' — re-bench on the actual 1650 via the proposed __main__ 'voice' subcommand before committing to the SLO.

VRAM contention on 4GB is unaddressed and is the real risk: faster-whisper INT8 (~1-2.5GB) co-resident with Kokoro (~2-3GB inference footprint) does not fit comfortably in 4GB. Realistic config = small/base Whisper INT8 + Kokoro, or move STT (or TTS) to CPU. Pin a quantized small STT model and verify peak VRAM, not just steady-state.

Repo pin must be bumped: current sidecar/pyproject.toml has pipecat-ai>=0.0.50 (pre-1.0) plus a sounddevice>=0.5.0 pin under the 'voice' extra. The recommendation is right to bump to 1.0+ and switch sounddevice->pyaudio for the canonical LocalAudioTransport path; drop the sounddevice pin unless a custom transport is written.
Parakeet-vs-Whisper 'faster' claim is unverified for this specific GPU and should be treated as a hypothesis to bench, not a given, on a 4GB Turing card.

dimensions.choice: Two-tier STT behind a single STT adapter: (1) DEFAULT local-first = faster-whisper large-v3-turbo INT8 in the Python sidecar for push-to-talk (record→release Ctrl+Shift+Space→transcribe), accepting ~0.8-2s final-transcript latency on the GTX 1650; (2) CLOUD FAST LANE = Groq whisper-large-v3-turbo via the existing OpenRouter/Groq client for when network is up and the user wants minimum latency. Make it a runtime-selectable strategy, not a rewrite.
corrections: config.py is MISCHARACTERIZED: it contains NO settings dataclass/schema -- it is only load_local_env() that reads .env files into os.environ. There is no existing config object to 'add stt_engine to.' The seam must FIRST introduce a settings schema (e.g. a Settings dataclass or pydantic-settings) before stt_engine/stt_model/stt_compute_type can be selected. As written, 'select via config.py' has nothing to select against.

PIN ctranslate2>=4.8.0. The Windows+Python-3.13 local lane is real but FRAGILE: the cp313-cp313-win_amd64 wheel only landed in CTranslate2 4.8.0 on 2026-06-06 (verified live via PyPI JSON). Any older pin (4.4-4.7 era, common in existing faster-whisper installs) has NO cp313 wheel and the local DEFAULT lane will fail to install on this Python 3.13 machine. Also requires cuDNN 9 / CUDA 12.3+ (CTranslate2 4.5.0+ dropped cuDNN 8); install nvidia-cudnn-cu12>=9 and nvidia-cublas-cu12 explicitly.

IPC TRANSPORT GAP not flagged: the current ipc.py JsonLineIpcServer is JSON-lines over stdio with only 'health'/'utterance'/'browser.task' methods. It has NO binary path. process_audio(pcm: bytes) cannot be driven by raw PCM over this transport without base64-encoding (significant bloat over stdio for multi-second 16kHz audio) or a separate audio side-channel. Add an explicit 'audio' IPC method that carries base64 PCM (or move capture+STT entirely into the Python sidecar via sounddevice and pass only text out). The rec's 'mic capture belongs in ipc.py' under-specifies this.

Groq routing: the OpenAI-compatible CHAT client in environment.py (the 'openai' SDK path) is the WRONG endpoint for STT. Groq Whisper is an audio-transcription endpoint, not chat. Good news: OpenRouter added /api/v1/audio/transcriptions in 2026 with Groq as a listed provider, so routing Groq Whisper through the global OpenRouter gateway IS legitimate (the rec's 'OpenRouter/Groq' is now defensible) -- but the GroqWhisperEngine must POST to the audio/transcriptions endpoint, not reuse _response_for or chat.completions. Confirm whether Frank wants direct Groq (GROQ_API_KEY, present in environment.py SECRET_KEYS) or OpenRouter-proxied Groq; both work, pick one.

Deepgram key claim is slightly wrong: environment.py SECRET_KEYS ALREADY lists DEEPGRAM_API_KEY as a known slot (so the integration scaffolding anticipates it). The rec says Deepgram is 'not currently in Frank's inventory' -- the slot exists; only whether it is POPULATED is open. Minor.

Deepgram Nova-3 p95 claim is slightly stronger than documented: verified ranges are ~150-300ms server-side / 200-500ms client-side WITH interim results, but Deepgram does not formally publish p50/p95 ms guarantees (the '~450ms median / <300ms p95' figure is third-party/empirical, not vendor-spec). Treat as 'sub-300ms-class interim' rather than a contracted SLA.

Minor over-pessimism on local speed: the rec says INT8 'runs on plain CUDA cores, not Tensor cores' implying no acceleration. Turing 7.5 actually has DP4A integer-dot-product acceleration that CTranslate2 INT8 uses, so local turbo is likely a bit faster than the rec's pessimistic floor. The rec's 0.8-2s-for-3s estimate is conservative/safe, which is the right direction -- no change needed, just note local may comfortably beat it.

dimensions.choice: Two-tier: LOCAL DEFAULT = Kokoro-82M (kokoro-onnx) for privacy + zero per-min cost; CLOUD QUALITY/SPEED TIER = Cartesia Sonic 3.5 streaming (lowest verified P50 188ms TTFA) selected when the router's FAST/voice tier wants flagship voice or when local GPU is contended.
corrections: SEAM async mismatch (load-bearing): ipc.py and pipeline.process_text are fully SYNCHRONOUS today (blocking `for line in stdin`, sync `stdout.write`). The proposed `async def stream()` / `async def process_voice()` AsyncIterator contract requires introducing an asyncio event loop and an async IPC path that does not exist yet. The seam understates this — it is the single biggest piece of real work, not a drop-in.

SEAM router overstatement: router.decide(text) is a keyword matcher returning a RouteTier; it has NO 'flagship voice' intent and emits no engine selection. 'router.py line 89 RouteTier.FAST is the trigger that selects local-vs-cloud TTS' is misleading — line 89 is merely the default fall-through. Engine selection logic (intent->engine) must be added net-new; the router does not gate TTS today. Recommend a separate TTS-selection function fed by config + optional intent, not overloading RouteTier.

SEAM ipc.py streaming: current server writes exactly one JSON-line response per request (request/response). Emitting tts.frame/tts.done mid-request needs a push/streaming protocol change to stdout, not just new message types. Verify the Rust Tauri shell can consume a multi-frame stream over the same stdio channel.

Kokoro GTX 1650 latency is UNVERIFIED on this exact card. Corroborated only generically (GPU 100-300ms, faster-than-realtime short utterances; A100 RTF 0.03). The '150-400ms first chunk on GTX 1650' is plausible-but-optimistic and MUST be measured before trusting it as the default that meets the <=800ms budget — especially under Whisper GPU contention on a 4GB card. Also confirm onnxruntime-gpu + CUDA actually initializes on GTX 1650 (a known CUDNN_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR report exists for that GPU); CPU fallback (RTF ~0.45-0.51) still beats realtime but raises first-chunk time.

Kokoro does NOT natively stream (generate-per-utterance, kokoro-onnx v0.5.0 Jan 2026). The recommendation honestly flags this, but the sentence-chunking streaming wrapper is required engineering, identical in shape to the Orpheus clip-stitching it criticizes — so Kokoro's 'streaming' advantage over Orpheus is smaller than implied. Both need sentence-level orchestration.

ElevenLabs exact 288ms/28ms IQR could not be re-confirmed from a primary Coval table in this pass; independent sources confirm the DIRECTIONAL claim (Flash v2.5 ~75-150ms inference-only for <100 chars; real playable TTFA higher; tighter jitter than Cartesia). Treat 288ms as a reasonable production estimate, not a hard primary-sourced number.

Minor: Groq Orpheus demotion is fully VINDICATED by primary source (Groq docs): 200-char hard cap CONFIRMED, WAV-only CONFIRMED, REST /audio/speech (not websocket) with no documented streaming CONFIRMED. No correction needed there — flagging only that the recommendation's reasoning here is the most solid part.

dimensions.choice: deepagents 0.6.10 as the workflow/agent-loop engine, running on its bundled LangGraph 1.1.x substrate with a SqliteSaver checkpointer. Wire it behind the router so it only runs for the DELIBERATION and CLI_AGENT tiers; the FAST voice-chat tier never touches it and keeps its low-latency path.
corrections: OpenRouter wiring is WRONG as stated. deepagents 0.6.10 defaults to Anthropic (claude-sonnet-4-20250514) and reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; it does NOT auto-route through OpenRouter just because OPENAI_BASE_URL/OPENAI_API_KEY env vars are set. The seam MUST explicitly construct the model and pass it: model=ChatOpenAI(model='openai/gpt-5', base_url='https://openrouter.ai/api/v1', api_key=<OPENROUTER_API_KEY>) or init_chat_model('openai:<model>', base_url=..., api_key=...), then create_deep_agent(model=model, ...). Note LangChain's official guidance flags ChatOpenAI+base_url to non-OpenAI providers as best-effort (targets official OpenAI spec) but OpenRouter's /chat/completions is OpenAI-compatible and works in practice. Also: OPENROUTER_API_KEY (not OPENAI_API_KEY) is the correct key per global doctrine; per machine memory GEMINI_API_KEY also holds an OpenRouter-format key, so do not rely on the google-genai path.

Security pin is MISATTRIBUTED. The SQLi->RCE chain is real (CVE-2025-67644 SQLi CVSS 7.3 + CVE-2026-28277 msgpack deserialization), but the fix lives in the checkpoint packages, not core langgraph: upgrade langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite>=3.0.1 (latest 3.1.0) AND langgraph-checkpoint>=3.0. Pinning the fix to 'langgraph>=1.0.10' is incorrect framing; the >=1.0.10 floor is fine for other reasons but is not where the RCE patch is. The recommendation's langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite>=3.0.3 pin is safe. Add an explicit langgraph-checkpoint>=3.0 pin.

FILE-MAP ERROR carried from the brief: cognition/ contains ONLY router.py (verified on disk). pipeline.py, ipc.py, config.py, environment.py, browser.py live at the PACKAGE ROOT (sidecar/src/starlight_voice/), not under cognition/. The new module should be cognition/workflows.py, but the edits to _response_for and IPC target root-level pipeline.py and ipc.py. Method/enum names are correct: _response_for, process_text, RouteTier.DELIBERATION and RouteTier.CLI_AGENT all exist as claimed.

LATENCY claim is safe but VACUOUS at current repo state: there is no STT->LLM->TTS streaming path yet. pipeline.py is an explicit text-first skeleton (health() reports voice_loop: False, 'future Pipecat audio graph'). The engine genuinely cannot touch a first-audio budget that does not exist yet, so the P50<=800ms protection is correct by construction but unproven. Validate after the audio loop lands.

DEPENDENCY WEIGHT confirmed heavier than 'pure-Python library' framing: deepagents 0.6.10 hard-depends on langchain>=1.3.9, langchain-core>=1.4.7, langchain-anthropic>=1.4.6, langchain-google-genai>=4.2.5, langsmith>=0.8.11, wcmatch>=10.1. The anthropic/google integration packages install but stay unused on the OpenRouter path (dead weight, not breakage). The fallback to raw LangGraph does NOT shed this tree since langchain-core/langsmith still come in.

Known bug deepagents #554 (subagent interrupt resume fails for edit/reject, only approve works) affects SUBAGENTS only, not the top-level agent. The three target workflows are single top-level agents, so they are unaffected today; but if morning_brief/file_triage later spawn sub-agents with their own approval gates, edit/reject resume will silently break until upstream fixes it. Keep approval gates on the top-level agent.

dimensions.choice: Keep the four tested primitives FROZEN as contracts (CognitionRouter.decide, JsonLineIpcServer envelope, AgentPipeline.process_text seam, EnvironmentDoctor/load_local_env), and build the entire audio path net-new behind them. Do NOT follow PLAN.md/SPEC.md literally — they are aspirational and contradict the real code in two load-bearing ways: (1) the IPC is request/response, not a streaming SidecarMessage enum; (2) there are no adapters and pipeline responses are canned strings. The router already gives you tier classification for free; the missing piece is the dispatch+audio behind each tier.
corrections: LATENCY IS TIGHT, NOT COMFORTABLE — and the recommendation under-accounts for the LLM leg in the first-audio budget. The SPEC's own component budget (turn-detection 90ms + STT partial 300ms + TTS TTFA 150ms = 540ms) omits the LLM TTFT contribution to FIRST AUDIO. You cannot speak the first TTS chunk until the LLM has emitted its first token. Verified June 2026 numbers, summed realistically: Deepgram Flux EOT ~300ms (median) + LLM TTFT + Cartesia TTFA. Best case LLM ~220-240ms (OpenRouter 50-70ms routing overhead + Cerebras ~170ms TTFT for Llama 3.3 70B) gives ~630-650ms — under 800ms P50. But a real-world OpenRouter TTFT measurement was 640ms (opper.ai benchmark), and independent Cartesia P50 was 188ms with 100ms IQR (wide variance). Realistic sum ~1100-1150ms — that BLOWS the 800ms P50 and lands mid-P95. Verdict: 800ms P50 is ACHIEVABLE but only with near-optimal LLM dispatch and tight network RTT; it is NOT a safe default assumption. The e2e benchmark probe in seam step 7 is therefore the single most important deliverable — build it FIRST as a gate, not last.

OPENROUTER vs CEREBRAS-DIRECT IS AN UNRESOLVED TENSION the recommendation papers over. Global doctrine mandates OpenRouter; the sub-800ms budget assumes Cerebras-class 170ms TTFT. Verified: Cerebras IS reachable on OpenRouter, BUT it is 'only available via proxy' (Cerebras support docs) adding marginal latency ON TOP of the 50-70ms OpenRouter routing overhead, and routing is not guaranteed to land on Cerebras unless you pin the provider via OpenRouter's provider-routing 'order'/'only' params. CORRECTION to seam step 2 (llm.py): must explicitly pin provider to Cerebras (or another sub-200ms-TTFT provider) in the OpenRouter request body for the FAST tier, otherwise OpenRouter may route to a 600ms+ TTFT provider and silently break the SLA. The router classifies tier correctly, but llm.py owns the provider-pin-by-tier decision — make it explicit.

PROVIDER VERSIONS IN SPEC.md ARE STALE (provider choice is delegated to cloud-fallback dimension, so this is a SPEC bug not a recommendation flaw, but flag it): SPEC.md hardcodes Cartesia Sonic-2, which is DEPRECATED with a June 1, 2026 cutover that has ALREADY PASSED (today is June 15, 2026). Current model is Sonic-3.5 (sonic-3.5-2026-05-04, ~75-90ms TTFA WebSocket). tts.py adapter must target Sonic-3.5, not Sonic-2 — any Sonic-2 code will hit deprecation. Deepgram Flux (<300ms EOT, integrated turn detection) and Cerebras Llama (~170ms TTFT) claims VERIFY as current and real.

PYPROJECT CLAIM IS PARTLY MISLEADING. Recommendation seam step 1 says 'Real deps are currently empty ([]); the runtime cannot import anything today.' The top-level `dependencies = []` is literally empty, BUT optional-dependencies are FULLY POPULATED: voice=[pipecat-ai>=0.0.50, sounddevice>=0.5.0], providers=[anthropic, openai], browser=[browser-use]. So the install path already exists as extras — the seam is `uv pip install -e .[voice,providers]`, not 'add deps from scratch'. Also: requires-python is already `>=3.12` which ACCOMMODATES 3.13 (verified: pipecat-ai and sounddevice both ship CPython 3.13.7 wheels as of Jan-Feb 2026). The seam's implication that pyproject needs a Python-version bump is wrong — no change needed there. The real change is making the `voice`+`providers` extras default-installed for Frank's machine, which the recommendation does correctly identify.

SidecarMessage STREAMING-ENUM MISMATCH CLAIM VERIFIED AS CORRECT. Confirmed: tauri/src/sidecar.rs is one-shot Command::output() for 'health' only — no persistent piped child, no SidecarMessage enum in actual code. The SidecarMessage tagged-enum (PttPressed/UtteranceText/Status/Shutdown) exists ONLY in docs/PLAN.md as aspirational design (lines 1094+), not in the codebase. ipc.py is strictly blocking request/response. The recommendation's central thesis — freeze the real {id,method,params}->{id,ok,result} envelope and ADD an id-less notification line shape for server-push — is sound and does NOT break test_ipc.py (verified: tests call handle_line() directly with health/utterance/unknown-method assertions; they never exercise serve()'s streaming loop, so adding notification emission to serve() is contract-safe).

FALLBACK (in-process audio in sidecar, Rust = PTT+tray+lifecycle only) IS THE STRONGER PRIMARY, NOT JUST A FALLBACK. Streaming raw/encoded TTS audio chunks as base64 over a JSON-lines stdio pipe is workable but adds encode/decode + line-buffering overhead on the hot path and risks head-of-line blocking against the same stdout used for RPC responses. Running mic->STT->router->LLM->TTS->speakers fully in-process via sounddevice (verified Windows/WASAPI + Python 3.13 support) keeps audio off the stdio boundary entirely and is the lower-latency, lower-complexity path to the 800ms SLA. Recommend ELEVATING the fallback to the default and keeping IPC to coarse control (listen.start/stop, status) — this also de-risks the persistent-piped-child rewrite of sidecar.rs (seam step 6), which is the biggest net-new Rust lift.

dimensions.choice: Ship BOTH as one bounded sprint, wired through the existing seams — do NOT add new frameworks. (1) PROACTIVE: a batch 'overnight analyzer' run by Windows Task Scheduler at 04:30 (matching the StarlightSecretScan slot) that scans git state across active repos, the Google Calendar MCP, and the pending-approval queue, scores candidates with a deterministic weighted function, makes ONE cheap OpenRouter synthesis call (gemini-3-flash or deepseek-r1) to phrase them, and writes memory/voice/brief-YYYY-MM-DD.json. On first push-to-talk of the morning (or wake-word later) the operator reads the cached brief through the realtime TTS lane so it still hits P50<=800ms first-audio. (2) DISPATCH: replace the dead stub at pipeline.py:52 (RouteTier.CLI_AGENT) with a real backend — add complexity_score() + a fleet table using the CORRECTED June-2026 model IDs, emit an existing v1 handoff-packet, gate on Tier A/B/C, then async-spawn the chosen CLI via the cl/cd/agy/oa command grid. FIRST corrective action: fix CODING_AGENTS_REGISTRY.md model IDs (it is already staged on the working branch) and remove Gemini CLI as a live target before its June 18 2026 shutdown — promote Antigravity (agy) to the Gemini-family seat.
corrections: FALSE CLAIM: registry is NOT 'already M-staged on the working branch.' git status/git diff on agents/CODING_AGENTS_REGISTRY.md are both EMPTY; the file still holds the stale IDs (claude-3-5-sonnet, gpt-4o, grok-2, gemini-1.5-pro). The only M-staged files in SIS are scripts/agy-tools.ps1 and scripts/machine-sentinel.ps1. The 'first corrective action' is entirely TODO, not staged. Apply the edit fresh.

STALE BENCHMARK: Terminal-Bench claims are wrong. Recommendation says 'Opus 4.8 #2 @78.9%' and 'GPT-5.5 #1 @83.4%.' Per tbench.ai 2.1 (updated 2026-06-09): Claude Fable 5 LEADS at 88.0%, GPT-5.5 = 83.4%, Opus 4.8 = 82.7% (NOT 78.9%, NOT #2). The fleet table omits Fable 5, the actual coding-tier leader. The 7-10 complexity seat should default to Fable 5 (claude-fable-5), with Opus 4.8 as the deep-prose alternate, per the global doctrine which already names Fable 5 the default agentic model.

STALE DEP PIN: 'LangGraph 0.4.x (June 2026)' is wrong. Current LangGraph is 1.2.x as of June 2026. The pin 'langgraph>=0.4' will resolve to 1.x, which has breaking API changes vs 0.4.x patterns — pin explicitly (e.g. langgraph>=1.2,<2) and write against the 1.x API, not 0.4 tutorials. Python 3.13 support IS real (LangChain changelog confirms 3.10-3.14).

SCOPE OVER-SPEC: LangGraph is not load-bearing for either feature as scoped. The proactive analyzer (subprocess git scan + weighted scorer + one httpx OpenRouter call) and dispatch (complexity_score + fleet table + fire-and-forget pwsh spawn) are plain Python. Adding langgraph as an MVP dep buys nothing the seam uses. Defer it until a real multi-node loop exists behind the router; ship the sprint with httpx + ulid-py only.

P50<=800ms HEADROOM is tight, not free. Gradium 2026 benchmark: streaming-TTS TTFA floor is ~214ms (median, optimized WebSocket+token-stream) up to ~324ms for ElevenLabs Flash — and that is TTS-only, measured to PLAYABLE audio not container headers. For the CACHED-brief path (no live LLM) 800ms is achievable; for any live-LLM-first-token path it is not. Keep the brief strictly pre-computed to brief.json as specified, and measure TTFA past container metadata (WAV/Ogg/ID3 headers can falsely report ~50ms).

MINOR: pyproject requires-python is '>=3.12' (workspace) — fine for 3.13, but the sidecar pyproject the recommendation says to 'uv add into' was not located at the cited path; sidecar deps live in the workspace pyproject.toml (dependencies=[] today). Confirm the exact pyproject before uv add.

synthesis.summary: Validated buildable architecture for closing the Starlight Voice realtime loop on Frank's GTX 1650 laptop by HARDENING the existing C:/Users/frank/starlight-voice repo. Build the audio path NET-NEW behind four FROZEN tested primitives (CognitionRouter.decide, JsonLineIpcServer envelope, AgentPipeline.process_text, EnvironmentDoctor/load_local_env) - NOT following the aspirational PLAN.md/SPEC.md (their SidecarMessage streaming enum and Sonic-2 references are stale/nonexistent). All five verifier verdicts HOLD WITH CORRECTIONS, applied below. Biggest architectural change is sync-to-async: ipc.py and pipeline.py are fully synchronous request/response today; the streaming voice loop is async - so the in-process audio path (mic to STT to LLM to TTS to speakers entirely inside the Python sidecar via PyAudio/WASAPI; Rust shell handles only PTT hotkey plus tray plus lifecycle) is ELEVATED to primary, keeping audio off the stdio boundary. P50 first-audio 800ms is achievable but TIGHT on this 4GB-VRAM no-Tensor-core card and MUST be benchmarked on-device FIRST (the __main__ voice subcommand plus benchmarks/run.py probe is the load-bearing first deliverable). Critical latency risk: the LLM first-token leg is omitted from SPEC budget; the OpenRouter request MUST explicitly pin a sub-200ms-TTFT provider (Cerebras) per-tier in llm.py or the doctrine-mandated gateway silently breaks the SLA. VRAM contention on 4GB is the real risk: Whisper INT8 plus Kokoro do not comfortably co-reside, so plan to run STT or TTS on CPU and measure PEAK VRAM before locking Kokoro default. deepagents 0.6.10 sits behind the router for DELIBERATION/CLI_AGENT/WORKFLOW tiers only (off audio path); its model MUST be explicitly constructed as ChatOpenAI with base_url OpenRouter or it silently defaults to Anthropic. Proactive morning brief and async fleet dispatch are wiring jobs on existing seams (CLI_AGENT stub pipeline.py line 52, handoff-packet v1), correcting stale registry IDs (route complexity 7-10 to Fable 5, the actual Terminal-Bench leader) and dropping LangGraph from the MVP (httpx plus ulid-py suffice).

final_stack.choice: Pipecat 1.0+ pipeline running IN-PROCESS inside the Python sidecar (LocalAudioTransport via PyAudio/WASAPI), driven by a new async voice_loop.py. Rust/Tauri shell does ONLY PTT hotkey (Ctrl+Shift+Space) plus tray plus lifecycle; audio never crosses the stdio IPC boundary.
final_stack.fallback: If Pipecat 1.0 API churn or PyAudio/WASAPI is unstable on this laptop, hand-rolled async loop (sounddevice capture, faster-whisper, OpenRouter stream, Kokoro stream) reusing CognitionRouter; loses Smart Turn v3. Do NOT switch to LiveKit (WebRTC overhead) or Vocode (losing momentum).

final_stack.choice: Pipecat LocalSmartTurnAnalyzerV3 (ONNX, CPU-only, ~12-65ms). PTT gates transport input first; semantic turn detection layered for later wake-word/barge-in.
final_stack.fallback: Plain Silero VAD endpointing (bundled with faster-whisper) if Smart Turn v3 ONNX runtime misbehaves on Windows.

final_stack.choice: faster-whisper large-v3-turbo INT8 on CUDA via Pipecat WhisperSTTService - PTT clip transcribe (~0.8-2s final on GTX 1650; no mid-utterance partials needed for PTT).
final_stack.fallback: Drop to base/small.en INT8, or move STT to CPU if Kokoro plus Whisper exceed 4GB VRAM. MUST bench peak VRAM before locking.

final_stack.choice: Groq whisper-large-v3-turbo via OpenRouter /api/v1/audio/transcriptions endpoint (NOT chat.completions) - sub-1s finals, beats local on the 1650 when network is up.
final_stack.fallback: Deepgram Nova-3 streaming WebSocket (DEEPGRAM_API_KEY slot already in environment.py) ONLY if true sub-300ms interim partials become a hard requirement. Defer Parakeet/NeMo until a Tensor-core GPU.

final_stack.choice: OpenRouterLLMService(base_url=OPENROUTER_BASE_URL, api_key=OPENROUTER_API_KEY) streaming, with the FAST tier request body explicitly PINNING a sub-200ms-TTFT provider (Cerebras via OpenRouter provider order/only params) - provider-pin-by-tier lives in llm.py, NOT the router.
final_stack.fallback: If OpenRouter provider tail latency blows P95, pin a different colocated fast provider; last resort a full cloud S2S voice lane (OpenAI gpt-realtime / Gemini Live) behind the router as DELIBERATION/fallback voice only - never the local primary.

final_stack.choice: Kokoro-82M (kokoro-onnx, Apache-2.0) streamed sentence-by-sentence from the LLM token stream - zero per-min cost, zero egress, ~2-3GB. GATED: first-chunk latency on GTX 1650 under Whisper contention is UNVERIFIED and must be measured before locking as default.
final_stack.fallback: Promote Cartesia to default if Kokoro misses budget on-device; Piper (MIT, CPU, never contends for GPU) is the always-works offline degraded tier.

final_stack.choice: Cartesia Sonic 3.5 streaming WebSocket (P50 ~188ms TTFA, lowest independently-verified; true bidirectional input-streaming pairs with token-stream).
final_stack.fallback: ElevenLabs Flash v2.5 stream-input (tightest 28ms IQR = safest P95, highest subjective quality). Bake-off Cartesia vs ElevenLabs vs Inworld Realtime TTS-2 before locking cloud default. NOT Groq Orpheus as primary (200-char cap, WAV-only, no true REST streaming).

final_stack.choice: deepagents 0.6.10 (cloned at C:/Users/frank/deepagent/libs/deepagents) on bundled LangGraph 1.x plus SqliteSaver, BEHIND the router for DELIBERATION/CLI_AGENT/WORKFLOW tiers only - off the realtime audio path. Model MUST be explicitly constructed: ChatOpenAI(model=openai/..., base_url=openrouter, api_key=OPENROUTER_API_KEY) then create_deep_agent(model=model,...), else silently defaults to Anthropic. interrupt_on with allowed_decisions approve/edit/reject/respond maps to approval gates. Keep gates on TOP-LEVEL agents (subagent edit/reject resume broken upstream, deepagents issue 554).
final_stack.fallback: Drop to RAW LangGraph 1.x (interrupt() plus SqliteSaver) for any workflow needing custom topology - same substrate, no migration. Avoid LlamaIndex/Burr (second ecosystem).

open_risks: P50 800ms first-audio is TIGHT, not comfortable, on the GTX 1650 (Turing, 4GB, no Tensor cores). Realistic summed latency (OpenRouter TTFT ~640ms observed plus STT/turn plus Cartesia ~188ms with 100ms IQR) can land ~1100ms = blows P50, mid-P95. ONLY holds with near-optimal provider-pinned LLM dispatch plus tight RTT. Must be benched on-device before the SLO is treated as met.

VRAM contention on 4GB: faster-whisper INT8 (~1.5GB) plus Kokoro (~2-3GB inference) do NOT comfortably co-reside. Likely need STT or TTS on CPU. Measure PEAK VRAM. onnxruntime-gpu has a reported CUDNN_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR on GTX 1650 - verify GPU init or fall back to CPU (Kokoro CPU RTF ~0.45-0.51 still beats realtime but raises first-chunk time).

Doctrine vs latency tension: global doctrine mandates OpenRouter; sub-800ms assumes Cerebras-class ~170ms TTFT. OpenRouter routes to Cerebras only via proxy plus only if provider explicitly pinned in request body. Unpinned, OpenRouter may silently route to a 600ms-plus provider and break the SLA.

Kokoro does NOT natively stream (generate-per-utterance) - needs the same sentence-chunking wrapper it beats Orpheus on; its streaming advantage is smaller than implied. Both need sentence-level orchestration.

Sync-to-async migration of ipc.py/pipeline.py is the one real architectural change and the riskiest seam; mitigated by elevating in-process audio (Rust = PTT plus tray only) so audio never crosses stdio and the persistent-piped-child rewrite of sidecar.rs is avoided for MVP.

deepagents pulls heavy LangChain 1.x tree (langchain-anthropic plus langchain-google-genai dead weight on OpenRouter path); model MUST be explicitly constructed or it silently routes to Anthropic. GEMINI_API_KEY slot holds an OpenRouter-format key per machine memory - do not rely on the google-genai path.
